envName.description: The NAME of an environment variable: letters, digits and underscores. A value is refused.

url.description: An http or https URL with a host and no credentials: a password in a URL is a secret in the file, and a secret is named, never carried.

description: The configuration of access-issuer: the issuer, the console and the directory hub, one process. Secrets are never in this file: a field ending in ...Env holds the NAME of the environment variable that holds the secret, and a field ending in ...File holds a path. Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

adminPasswordEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the hub's recovery password, for a run outside a cluster. Unset generates one and prints it once.

allowInsecure.description: Accept a plain-http issuer URL, for a local run.

audience.description: The audience a consumer's token must carry.

consumersFile.description: The file naming the ServiceAccounts that may call it. None named admits nobody in a cluster.

audit.description: The audit installation this service records to. Unset keeps the trail in the log only.

audience.description: The client whose audience the Audit page's tokens carry.

forwardedForTrustedHops.description: How many of the deployment's own proxies append to X-Forwarded-For; zero records the peer.

queryURL.description: The query service, for the console's Audit page. Needs `writer`.

tokenFile.description: This workload's projected service-account token, presented on every call.

clientSecretsDir.description: A directory holding one file per confidential client, named after the client id, each the client's secret. Read per call, so a rotated Secret takes effect without a restart.

cluster.description: Names this cluster in a ServiceAccount's subject. A pod cannot discover it; unset keeps the older unqualified subject.

console.description: Where the console is published, for the sign-in that starts there.

client.description: The client id the console signs in as.

origin.description: The console's origin, when it is not the issuer's.

demo.description: Two tenants held in memory, which need no credential and no network.

exchange.description: What the token exchange verifies workloads against.

audience.description: The audience a workload token must be minted for. Defaults to `release`, so two issuers in one cluster cannot accept each other's proofs.

awsFile.description: The file naming the AWS accounts, each by its published key set. Read once at start.

clustersFile.description: The file naming the federated clusters, each by its published key set. Read once at start.

freshness.description: How the directory's snapshot is kept current.

freshnessWindow.description: How old a snapshot may be and still be answered from.

probeInterval.description: How often the directory is probed.

refreshInterval.description: How often a snapshot is refreshed.

github.description: What the service knows of GitHub.

catalogueFile.description: The file declaring every GitHub App. A malformed one stops the service.

owners.description: The organisations whose repositories' CI tokens are verified. None names none: an empty list would admit every repository there is.

runnerTiers.description: The tiers an operator may create a runner App for: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 16, each once.

groupsScoping.description: How far this installation has moved toward per-audience `groups` scoping: `off`, `report` or `enforce`.

inCluster.description: Prove recovery against the cluster the pod runs in. Set by a deployment that turns recovery on.

issuerURL.description: The issuer: baked into every token and every relying party's trust, so there is no default. No trailing slash is kept.

lifetimes.description: How long what the issuer hands out lives.

absolute.description: A session, at most. Positive, and at least `token`: a session has to end SOMETIME after sign-in, and an access token cannot outlive the session that grants it.

hold.description: How long a removal is held before it takes effect.

session.description: The console's own session cookie, capped at `absolute`.

login.description: How a person signs in to the console.

directory.description: Sign in with the corporate directory.

forwarded.description: A sign-in an authenticating proxy has already done.

emailHeader.description: The header that carries the signed-in address.

oauthClient.description: The OAuth client registered once with the directory backend: it drives both admin consent and operator sign-in.

id.description: The client id, for a local run. Not a secret.

idFile.description: A file holding the client id.

idKey.description: The key of the id in that Secret.

secretEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the client secret, for a local run.

secretFile.description: A file holding the client secret.

secretKey.description: The key of the secret in that Secret.

secretName.description: The Kubernetes Secret the client is declared in, which the console shows and cannot change.

overlayFile.description: The file of declared workspaces, mounted.

policyDir.description: The directory the policy is mounted at. Unset is the built-in two groups, or the demonstration policy under `demo`.

publicRootURL.description: The host's root, never carrying the console's mount: the bootstrap surface stays there. Unset follows `publicURL`.

publicURL.description: Where a browser reaches the console, including its mount. The admin-consent redirect URI and the values the setup steps show are built from it. Default http://localhost:8081.

recovery.description: The sign-in that needs no directory: a token for a ServiceAccount, proven against the cluster. Unset is off for the issuer and, for the hub, on.

audience.description: The audience its token must carry.

enabled.description: Turn recovery on. Needs `inCluster`, `serviceAccount` and `audience` to be usable.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount whose token signs in.

release.description: The name this installation's objects carry: the Kubernetes object names (`<release>-github-orgs`, ...) and the prefix of its keys in a shared store. The chart requires it to be the release's full name.

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure. Unset follows the scheme the browser will use: https in the URL.

signingKey.description: The issuer's signing keys: provisioned, never minted here.

activationDelay.description: How long a newly published key waits before a replica signs with it. At least `pollInterval`.

additionalFiles.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, one file per algorithm.

file.description: The primary key. Unset generates one for this process, which a local run may do and nothing else should.

overlap.description: How long a rotated key stays published. Unset is `lifetimes.token` plus a margin for clock skew.

pollInterval.description: How often the files are re-read.

slack.description: What the service knows of Slack.

catalogueFile.description: The file declaring every Slack App. A malformed one stops the service.

store.description: Where what an operator connected is kept: `memory` keeps nothing (a restart is a fresh installation), `kubernetes` keeps it in this namespace.

valkey.description: The shared store for logins in progress and snapshots. Unset keeps both in memory, correct for one replica.

cluster.description: Speak the cluster protocol. A plain single server needs it off.

passwordEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the password.

title: access-issuer
